positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter states that because complex models are opaque even to many developers and users, no party currently stands to be accountable when data breaches or inaccurate outputs used in health practice cause harm. This accountability vacuum is the central worry.
positions.requested_fda_action: The commenter asks that AI manufacturers be held financially and legally accountable for all failures, data problems, and harms caused by these devices, rather than leaving responsibility undefined.

gap_explanations.distributed_accountability: The comment asserts that model opacity across developers and users leaves no identifiable responsible party when harm occurs, and asks that liability be concentrated on manufacturers.
gap_explanations.cybersecurity_as_safety: It treats data breaches alongside inaccurate outputs as sources of patient harm requiring accountability, linking security failures to clinical consequences.

positions.public_summary: Commenter argues model opacity leaves no accountable party when data breaches or inaccurate outputs cause harm in health practice. Beyond FDA's framing of preserving manufacturer accountability in postmarket roles, the commenter asks that AI manufacturers bear full financial and legal liability for all resulting harms.
positions.source_passage: Finally, the "black box" nature of complex models where the actually workings of the AI remain unknown to most of the developers and users presents an issue where, if there were data breeches or inaccurate information used in health practices which results in harm, there currently is no-one who stands to be accountable for such things. The AI manufacturers need to be held financially and legally accountable for ALL screw ups, data issues, or harm that these devices may do.
